title: Integration, Migration, and Documentation
objective: Unify governance projections, prove legacy migration and fail-closed rollback, complete directed integration coverage, and document v58 operations.
description: Closes the cross-command contract for status, flow, resume, export, machine output, compatibility, rollback, and operational documentation after the prior runtime slices land.
parallel_safe_reason: This closure slice is safe only after all runtime contracts and downstream gates are finalized.
must: Make approve, approvals, flow, status, resume, export, spec, slice, and PR surfaces consume the same canonical projection.
Keep JSON stdout machine-clean with stable nonlocalized keys, enums, statuses, codes, and exit semantics.
Apply common redaction to every new persisted, rendered, exported, and raw-evidence surface.
Read supported legacy state without write-on-read, invented data, or false phase advancement.
Provide explicit migration dry-run, apply, verify, and idempotent reapply behavior.
Use migrate dry-run for preview, confirmed migrate for apply plus post-verification, and doctor JSON for independent verification without adding a new command namespace.

Allow only the explicit migration writer to consume legacy-unverified evidence, then repeat the complete preflight and independently recheck writer and dependency compatibility before its first project write.
Label incomplete legacy evidence as legacy-unverified.
Provide rollback mode that disables v58 writers while retaining fail-closed readers and gates.
Block unsafe package downgrade while active v58-only conditions or decisions exist.
Persist schema-valid governance compatibility metadata and return the authorized stable compatibility codes at fail-closed boundaries.
Add directed integration fixtures for every AC-16 scenario and update only relevant public documentation.
not_included: Release, publish, deployment, or OTA steps.
Performance, load, or concurrency testing beyond the proven budget race.
acceptance: AC-13 is satisfied across all listed CLI, JSON, generation, and gate surfaces.
AC-14 is satisfied across persistence, rendering, export, and raw evidence.
AC-15 is satisfied for dual-read legacy behavior, explicit idempotent migration, and no false advancement.
AC-16 is satisfied for fail-closed rollback, downgrade guard, and all directed scenarios.
Migration dry-run performs no writes and apply plus reapply preserves valid governed and compatible unknown data.
Public documentation describes profiles, findings, budgets, decisions, migration, rollback, codes, and operator recovery without claiming release.
